caption: AI drafts misstate facts. These prompts help fact-check, verify sources, and tighten accuracy before publishing. Which claim will you fact-check first? #AIinBusiness #FactCheck #Productivity #Entrepreneurs

slides.title: AI drafts misstate facts
slides.body: AI drafts can read well but misstate facts. Use these five prompts to fact-check, verify sources, and tighten accuracy.

slides.title: 1. Diagnose
slides.body: Read [Draft text]. List each factual claim; mark status: true/likely/unclear/false; give a numbered citation suggestion.

slides.title: 2. Improve accuracy
slides.body: Rewrite [Draft text] to fix factual errors; keep tone; maintain citations; output: revised draft; ensure no new claims.

slides.title: 3. Apply checks
slides.body: Generate a checklist for the revised draft: citations, numbers, dates, names, provenance. Output: bullet list.

slides.title: 4. Verify sources
slides.body: For each cited claim, fetch a source or official doc; provide source type and link placeholder [URL].

slides.title: 5. Refine workflow
slides.body: Create a lasting policy to fact-check AI drafts: assign owners, cadence, sign-off rubric. Output: one-page policy draft.

slides.title: Takeaway
slides.body: Five-step QA reduces AI mistakes; adopt the checklist to trust drafts and speed up review.
